NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 10 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 15 · 10 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 12, 9:26 AM ET

Trey McBride is the top-projected tight end on the Week 10 DraftKings main slate at 16.6 DraftKings points for $7,100, against the Rams. George Kittle (15.9, $6,500) and Brock Bowers (14.5, $7,600) are next.

Colby Parkinson returns the most per dollar among tight ends projected for at least 7 points: 3.27 projected points per $1,000 at $3,000.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 12, 9:26 AM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 10

Trey McBride, ARI vs LAR ($7,100)

Trey McBride carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 16.6 DraftKings points at $7,100. That is 0.7 points clear of George Kittle. The model gives him 14.1 targets on 40.4 routes. The salary works out to 2.34 projected points per $1,000, 11th of 17 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations McBride averaged 16.7 points with a simulated floor of 4.0 and a ceiling of 43.8, and he holds 7% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Arizona is a 9.5-point underdog at home against the Rams, with an implied team total of 15 in a game totaled at 39.5.

George Kittle, SF at DAL ($6,500)

George Kittle projects 2nd at the position with 15.9 DraftKings points at $6,500. The model gives him 6.6 targets on 23.1 routes. The salary works out to 2.45 projected points per $1,000, 9th of 17 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Kittle averaged 15.9 points with a simulated floor of 3.6 and a ceiling of 42.3, and he holds 11% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. San Francisco is a 3.5-point favorite on the road against Dallas, with an implied team total of 29.5 in a game totaled at 55.5.

Value: Colby Parkinson, LAR at ARI ($3,000)

Colby Parkinson projects for 9.8 DraftKings points at $3,000, which works out to 3.27 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 17 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 4.4 targets on 12.7 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Parkinson averaged 9.7 points with a simulated floor of 0.0 and a ceiling of 31.3, and he holds 17% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. The Rams are a 9.5-point favorite on the road against Arizona, with an implied team total of 24.5 in a game totaled at 39.5.
